items.note: Compares three ways of using LLMs (free-form, direct generation, theory-structured) for design problem reframing and scores frame quality; the abstract names no no-AI arm and does not state assignment, so check for a control and randomization in the full text.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, Elsevier page blocked); the title suggests a study of GenAI-supported idea generation moderated by task breadth and cognitive flexibility, kept as experiment because the design is unknown.

Three studies across seven datasets and over 880,000 texts link LLM adoption to lower linguistic diversity, combining observational trends with LLM rewrites of human texts (no participants assisted by AI); journal version of arXiv 2502.11266.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, Elsevier page blocked); the title points to GenAI collaboration modes and employee innovation with a psychological-ownership outcome, which may be a survey or self-report study, so the full text must settle design and outcome.

Pre-registered randomized online experiment giving 310 researchers generative-AI suggestions while formulating research ideas, plus a 28-person follow-up; the outcomes are incorporation of suggestions and perceived novelty and impact, which may be self-rated, so check whether ideas are scored by outside raters (possible SSRN earlier version).

Exploratory quasi-experiment in engineering education comparing AI-assisted and human-only design teams on quantity, variety, uniqueness, and quality of design solutions; N not in abstract, and the unit is teams.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, Springer page behind login); the title points to a neuroimaging study of engineering design ideation with a human versus an AI partner, likely small, and it is unclear whether the output is scored.

Preregistered experiment with 77 students solving a complex creative problem with ChatGPT and 68 without, scoring quality, elaboration, and originality; abstract taken from the PsyArXiv preprint (9z2tc) because the Elsevier page was blocked, and it does not state the assignment method.

Preregistered meta-analysis of 106 experiments (370 effect sizes) on human-AI combinations, finding larger gains in content-creation tasks; it covers AI broadly (2020 to mid-2023), not only generative AI or creativity, so its fit as a synthesis for this section is borderline.

Small study (N=28) of collaborating with an AI agent framed as a conversational teammate on an ideation and ranking task; outcomes are creative self-efficacy and revision of idea rankings, the comparison condition is unclear, and N is below the 50-person threshold.
